title: Technology Feasibility Database — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Required science, components, cost estimates, constraints, and evidence of feasibility. The Technology Feasibility Database answers 'can this actually be built' with evidence: the science required (and whether it exists), the components needed (and whether they exist at the needed specs), cost estimates with the basis shown, the constraints (physics, regulation, supply), and the feasibility verdict with its reasoning. Most 'impossible' technologies fail on mundane grounds — no power source, no material, no economics — and this database checks the mundane first.

title: Technology Feasibility Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Feasibility dimensions: SCIENCE (do the principles exist? TRL-style maturity), COMPONENTS (do parts meet specs? COTS vs custom), PHYSICS (energy, materials, thermodynamics — hard limits like Carnot, Shannon, light speed), ECONOMICS (BOM cost vs price the market bears; learning curves), REGULATION (certifications, spectrum, safety), SUPPLY (can it be built at volume?). Method: Fermi estimation first (order-of-magnitude kills fast), then refine the binding constraint. Energy checks: E = P*t vs battery specific energy; power checks: P vs available sources. Verdict scale: feasible / feasible-with-conditions / infeasible-at-specs (with the feasible variant) / violates-physics. Evidence rule: every verdict cites the calculation or source behind each dimension. Re-evaluation: dates + trigger (what would change the verdict).

title: Technology Feasibility Database — Verification: tests and limitations
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Tests: Fermi test (estimates within an order of magnitude of known cases); energy test (budget math verified); verdict test (violations of hard limits always infeasible); determinism test. Limitations: estimates are approximate — stated; breakthroughs obsolete verdicts (re-evaluation schedule); economics need market data. Every verdict lists assumptions and date.

demo.title: Verification: trade-off scoring and sensitivity
demo.code: const opts={A:{perf:9,rel:6,simple:5},B:{perf:6,rel:9,simple:8}};const w={perf:0.5,rel:0.3,simple:0.2};function score(o){return o.perf*w.perf+o.rel*w.rel+o.simple*w.simple;}const sA=score(opts.A),sB=score(opts.B);const w2={perf:0.3,rel:0.5,simple:0.2};function score2(o){return o.perf*w2.perf+o.rel*w2.rel+o.simple*w2.simple;}const flip=score2(opts.B)>score2(opts.A);J({sA:+sA.toFixed(2),sB:+sB.toFixed(2),flip});assert(sA>sB&&flip,'tradeoff');
